Position Summary: The Strategic Finance Analytics Manager is a newly created role that builds and leads the financial modelling and analytics capability at the core of PointClickCare’s strategic finance function. The role delivers the models, tools, and decision support that enable leadership to drive profitability, optimize commercial strategy, and allocate resources with precision — with work that is highly visible to executive leadership, the Board, and investors. Positioned at the intersection of Finance, Strategy, and Go-to-Market, the near-term focus is Pricing & Monetization Analytics, while the broader mandate is to build scalable analytical frameworks applicable across any strategic finance domain the business identifies. A defining attribute of the role is the hands-on application of AI/ML to modernize and accelerate modelling, scenario generation, and reporting. Key Responsibilities: : Financial Modelling & Scenario Analysis. Build and maintain in-house financial and profitability models that evaluate the revenue and margin implications of strategic decisions, beginning with pricing and commercial strategy and expanding to other strategic finance domains. Run scenario and sensitivity analyses on packaging, pricing changes, GTM strategies, and investment trade-offs, measured against NRR, ARR, and contribution margin. AI-Led Modernization of the Analytics Toolkit. Apply AI/ML tools, including LLMs and predictive modelling, to accelerate modelling, scenario generation, and reporting, raising the speed and sophistication of decision support across the function. Build scalable, self-serve analytics tools that give Finance, Pricing, Sales Ops, and business unit leaders consistent, decision-ready intelligence. Pricing & Monetization Analytics. Evaluate pricing changes through quantitative modelling of customer, revenue, and margin impact across segments and geographies. Track pricing and monetization KPIs (discount compliance, revenue realization, contribution margin) against targets, and quantify the financial impact of commercial governance decisions including pricing policies, discount frameworks, and packaging structures. Executive & Profitability Reporting. Deliver regular profitability and commercial performance reporting to ELT and GTM leadership, including a measurement framework that tracks strategic initiative effectiveness, monetization outcomes, and contribution margin across products, segments, and geographies. Partner with FP&A and Sales Ops to integrate pricing and profitability analytics into the forecast and planning cycle, and with Revenue Assurance and Finance Ops to remediate pricing-related revenue risks. Stakeholder Engagement & Decision Support. Act as the primary analytical partner to Pricing, Sales Enablement, and business unit leaders on profitability decisions, translating complex analysis into clear, actionable recommendations. Present findings, models, and recommendations to senior leadership in executive-ready format, and contribute to Board and investor materials covering pricing strategy, monetization performance, and platform progress. Required Skills & Qualifications:: University degree in Finance, Business, Economics, or a related quantitative field 5–7 years in financial analysis, FP&A, or quantitative/strategic finance in a SaaS or technology environment. Exceptional financial modelling and scenario-analysis skills, with a demonstrated track record building revenue, profitability, or pricing models and translating them into decision support (the core qualification for the role). Hands-on experience applying AI/ML tools (including LLMs and predictive modelling) to accelerate and modernize modelling and reporting workflows — a defining attribute of the role, not a nice-to-have. Preferred Skills & Qualifications:: Pricing or monetization experience (an asset, not a requirement) Experience with BI tools (Power BI preferred) and executive-grade data visualization. The Data Analyst for Value-Based Insights (VBI) is responsible for transforming Medicare (CMS) claims data into metrics, benchmarks, and measures that power WellSky's VBI product for Home Health and Hospice providers and payers. This role builds and maintains claims-based data extracts and performance measures, translates CMS methodologies and regulatory rules into production analytics, and partners with product and engineering to deliver trusted, data-driven insights. The work is retrospective, methodology-driven, and directly tied to how agencies measure and improve value-based performance. Location: This is a remote position. Candidates located within 50 miles of WellSky’s headquarters in Overland Park, KS will join our WHQ community and participate in our in-office collaboration experience. Key Responsibilities: Build and maintain claims-based data extracts and measures from CMS data sources, including the Chronic Conditions Warehouse (CCW) and Limited Data Set (LDS), to support VBI Home Health and Hospice solutions. Develop and maintain performance measures such as HHVBP claims-based measures, MSPB-PAC, Functional Items, hospitalization/ER/PPH/DTC rates, utilization and efficiency metrics, length of stay, and composite/percentile scores. Interpret CMS regulations and annual Final Rules (e.g., HHVBP methodology, eTPS calculations) and translate measure specifications into accurate, reproducible SQL logic. Write and optimize SQL against large claims datasets in BigQuery; contribute to data pipelines, quarterly lookup-table refreshes, and extract automation. Produce referral pattern, competitive analysis, market/benchmark extracts, and validate outputs against CMS public benchmarks (e.g., Home Health Compare) and client expectations. Investigate data quality issues and metric discrepancies, and document methodology, data sources, and assumptions so results are auditable and repeatable. Prepare data for downstream BI/visualization layers (e.g., Sisense) and collaborate with product managers and engineers to define technical requirements and analytical interpretations. Perform other job duties as assigned. Direct experience working with Medicare/CMS claims data (e.g., CCW, LDS, LDS/RIF files, or comparable claims sources). Comfort with healthcare claims coding structures (e.g., ICD, HCPCS/CPT, revenue codes, DRGs). Ability to translate written specifications or methodologies into analytical logic and validate results for accuracy. Preferred Qualifications: Knowledge of Home Health and/or Hospice operations, post-acute care, or value-based care programs (e.g., HHVBP, HHVBP eTPS, hospice HIS/HOPE). Experience with CMS quality/value-based program methodologies and familiarity with reading CMS regulations/Final Rules. Hands-on experience with BigQuery (or a comparable cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake) and a BI tool such as Sisense, Tableau, or Power BI. Familiarity with risk adjustment or benchmarking concepts. Scripting experience (e.g., Python) for data transformation and automation. Job Expectations: Willing to work additional or irregular hours as needed, particularly around quarterly CMS data refreshes and annual Final Rule cycles. Job Description A bit about this role: The analysis behind Devoted's Medicare Advantage portfolio — which markets to grow in, which products to invest in, which benefit designs and cost structures actually work, creating those benefits — is driven today by a very small number of people. This team sits between claims analytics, product strategy, engineering, and actuarial, and is rebuilding how the portfolio and bid cycle work using agentic workflows and AI-assisted pipelines. This is not a reporting role. You'll own the strategic thinking and the pipework underneath it, often on the same day — there's no analyst between you and the data — and you'll see the whole picture — we'll expect you to have an opinion about it. Your Responsibilities and Impact will include: The analysis behind portfolio decisions . Product and service area mix — where we push growth and where we protect margin. You won't always be handed a question list; you'll help decide which questions matter. Cost and utilization work that answers the actual question . Decompose PMPM trend into utilization versus unit cost, build comparison groups you can defend when someone attacks them, and honestly size what a benefit change or network change will really do to claims. Independent financial judgment on benefit designs . Our own estimate of what a design does to revenue and cost, plus a clear sense of how much weight that estimate can bear. You'd own that work and be direct about its limits. Recommendations leadership can act on . Present data-backed recommendations to senior leaders regularly, including the CEO, and defend them live. Building the infrastructure, not just using it . We're rebuilding how the portfolio and bid cycle work with agentic workflows, AI-assisted code generation, and automated pipelines that turn what used to be weeks of manual work into something that runs overnight. This team is at the center of that build, and you'll push these tools into territory nobody here has tried yet. Go-to-market support . Once plans are filed, build the analyses go-to-market runs on, supporting marketing, sales, and brokers with a clear read on where our plans compete well and who they're built for. AEP monitoring . Track enrollment as it comes in against what the bid assumed: volume by plan and county, product mix, and the profile of who's choosing us. When something is moving the wrong way, you're the one who catches it early enough for us to do something about it. Being the person people come to . When someone needs to know whether a metric is built the right way or whether the data is being read correctly, you're the answer, not a ticket to another department. Required skills and experience: Six or more years in Medicare Advantage with your hands in the data . You know how claims are structured, what place-of-service and revenue codes tell you, the difference between allowed and paid, how completion factors work, and how risk adjustment feeds into all of it. You've been burned by a bad pull before, and you know what you check now because of it. Cost and utilization analytics . PMPM trend broken into utilization versus unit cost, clean comparison groups, sizing the impact of a benefit or network change. You know the difference between a number that moved and a number that means something. Strong SQL and real comfort in a large claims warehouse (Snowflake, Databricks, or similar). Analysis you've turned into strategy and defended . You've dug into claims data, formed your own point of view about what a company should do differently, and taken it to senior leadership — then handled the questions that came back, including the ones aimed at your method. You can hold your own with actuaries without being one. End-to-end ownership without scaffolding . Finding the data, sanity-checking it, modeling it, presenting it. The one-slide skill . You can put a complicated result on a single slide or Slack message without losing what's true about it. A collaborator, not a lone operator . This team is small enough that how you work with people matters as much as how good your analysis is. You share work before it's finished, you're direct without being sharp about it, and you're generous with what you know. We're remote and in constant communication. Nobody here is above any task, including the tedious ones. Desired skills and experience: Bid math . Every June, MA plans file a bid with CMS that sets the following year's revenue, benefits, and premiums — it's the annual event the entire portfolio is built around. If you know benchmarks, rebates, and benefit valuation, and you understand how bid assumptions constrain where the portfolio can go, that matters a great deal here. Having lived through a real bid cycle in some capacity counts for a lot. Optimization, Python, or actuarial training pointed at strategy . Benefit design, network configuration, or allocation problems framed and solved as constrained optimization. Python for analysis and modeling — pandas, statsmodels, scikit-learn, and comfort with clustering, regression, PCA, and trees. An ASA or FSA is not required, but if you have actuarial training and you've concluded you want strategy and product work over pure pricing, that's a profile we especially welcome. Fluent, practical use of AI tools . You already use AI in your analytical work as part of how you get things done and you're interested in pushing it further. Everyone on this team is expected to work this way. Job Description A bit about this role: We are seeking a meticulous and technically skilled Operations Senior Associate to lead the preparation, submission, and quality control of healthcare data and medical records to support normal operations and special projects. Special projects include CMS Risk Adjustment Data Validation (RADV) audits and Part C Improper Payment Measurement audits. This role is responsible for ensuring that all submissions to CMS are timely, accurate, compliant, and fully documented. Coordinate and direct day‑to‑day work activities of assigned team members for submission‑related tasks, ensuring priorities, timelines, and quality standards are met; partner with Devoted’s internal management team to align assignments and resolve resource issues. Conduct detailed quality assurance checks on all files, ensuring alignment with CMS specifications (naming conventions, file size limits, date visibility, provider credentials, and document legibility). Monitor and triage submission feedback, routing issues to coding, file prep, compliance, or audit teams as appropriate. Maintain meticulous tracking of submission status, metadata, and resolution notes in internal audit logs. Performance & Dashboards: Monitor weekly indicators (containment, escalation, complaints) and oversee production dashboards to track behavior independently. Diagnosis & Incident Response: Lead response for AI regressions; distinguish between model, prompt, or orchestration issues and drive post-mortems to closure. Continuous Improvement & Optimization: Run structured cycles (hypothesis, testing, rollout/rollback) for "mini-launches" like model swaps, prompt changes, and tool updates. Outcome Ownership: Deep personal accountability with a drive to own results rather than just producing recommendations. Job Description This role is fully remote and must be located within one of the contiguous 50 states. You must be able and willing to work 3x12s or 4x10s as long as Saturday and Sunday are covered. A bit about this role: The Digital Care Program and the Responsive Care Department are redefining how we connect with patients by delivering exceptional clinical care entirely through chat and other digital channels. Our mission is to meet patients where they are — online, in real time, and with the same compassion, expertise, and partnership they would expect in person. As an Advanced Practice Provider (NP or PA) focused on Digital Care, you will be a cornerstone of this mission. You’ll provide holistic, empathetic care to patients across multiple geographies, leveraging your clinical expertise and keen attention to detail to ensure their needs are understood and addressed. Digital Care APPs are not just providers; they are trusted partners, guiding patients through symptom management, chronic disease care, medication review, and coordination across their broader healthcare teams within and outside of Devoted — all within a digital-first experience. This role requires the agility to respond to real-time patient demand, manage evolving digital workflows, and flex across Responsive Care programs while maintaining exceptional clinical quality, safety, and patient experience. What Makes a Digital NP at Devoted Special: You are unmatched in clinical expertise, yet every interaction is guided by empathy and partnership. You anticipate patient needs, solve problems proactively, and go above and beyond at every step. You treat every patient as a whole person, considering both clinical and personal priorities. You are an expert in service, turning digital touchpoints into meaningful, human-centered care experiences. Required skills and experience: APP with three or more years working with experience in primary care, house calls, internal medicine, family medicine, geriatrics, palliative care and/or urgent care. Ability to review AI-generated responses for clinical accuracy and safety. Licensure and certification For Nurse Practitioners: active and in-good-standing RN and APRN licenses. For Physician Assistants: an active and in-good-standing Physician Assistant license. Role licensure and certification in good standing is required and the ability to get licensed in requested states within 90 days of hire date, starting at offer letter signing. You will be required to get licensed in additional states as needed. We believe in making it easy for you to focus on patient care. Devoted Health will cover all costs and provide full administrative support for obtaining and maintaining licenses in all required states. Desired skills and experience: Prior virtual care or telehealth experience preferred, with passion for engaging patients digitally. Experience working in real-time, queue-based, or high-volume telehealth clinical environments. Experience collaborating with interdisciplinary care teams and coordinating care remotely. Comfort managing complex or vulnerable patient populations in a digital-first setting. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, rapidly evolving environment with flexibility and curiosity. Responsibilities and Impact will include: Deliver exceptional, empathetic clinical care through real-time and asynchronous chat and other responsive care channels, supporting both the digital patient population and evolving queue-based needs across Responsive Care Department and the broader organization. Manage multiple concurrent and asynchronous patient conversations while maintaining clinical accuracy, timely documentation, and reliable follow-through. Guide and oversee patients’ medical management using a holistic framework (including the 5M approach: Mind, Mobility, Medications, Multicomplexity, Matters Most). Collaborate closely with patients’ primary care providers, specialists, and other teams such as pharmacy and specialty care to ensure continuity and comprehensiveness of care. Support patients’ care coordination with their family members and caregivers when appropriate, ensuring alignment with the patient’s priorities and goals. Provide thorough assessment, clinical guidance, and follow-up in response to patient-reported symptoms, medication questions, lab results, or new health concerns. Recognize when a patient’s needs cannot be safely or effectively addressed through chat and facilitate escalation to telephone, video, in-person, urgent, or emergency care as appropriate. Maintain ownership of patient needs through resolution or a clear, documented handoff. Maintain meticulous, accurate, and timely digital documentation in the electronic health record (EHR) in compliance with legal, ethical, and telehealth regulations. Continuously identify opportunities to improve patient experience and outcomes, leveraging digital workflows and proactive communication. Contribute to the improvement of digital workflows, standardized responses, escalation pathways, and quality standards. Occasionally support broader Devoted Medical service lines in line with program growth and team needs. Provide flexible clinical coverage across Responsive Care Department queues and on-call services as patient demand and operational priorities evolve. Adhere to all relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards, including patient privacy and telehealth regulations. ABOUT THE JOB The ACLU seeks applicants for a full-time two-year fellowship position in the Speech, Privacy and Technology Project of the ACLU’s National office in New York, NY. ICF seeks a Data and Quality Manager to support a nationwide legal services program serving Unaccompanied Alien Children (UAC) across the United States. Reporting to the Deputy Director of Operations, this position will lead the Data and Quality Team and oversee data collection, quality management, reporting, performance monitoring, compliance tracking, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) activities supporting the contract. The Data and Quality Manager serves as a key member of the project management team and collaborates closely with operations staff, legal service providers, technology teams, subcontractors, and federal stakeholders to ensure accurate, timely, and actionable data are available to support program oversight, contract compliance, and service delivery improvement. The purpose of this project is to provide legal services for unaccompanied children from Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) care and custody and to expand the legal community’s skills and capacity to provide immigration legal support. The Data and Quality Manager will oversee implementation and ongoing administration of LegalPath, the project's centralized case management and reporting platform, and ensure compliance with federal reporting requirements, data quality standards, quality assurance processes, and performance management expectations. As part of this position, the manager will develop dashboards, reports, analyses, and performance monitoring tools that transform complex operational, service delivery, quality, and outcome data into actionable insights that support decision-making, improve program performance, and strengthen service quality nationwide. Conduct trend analyses, root cause analyses, performance assessments, and predictive analyses to support operational improvements and decision making. Develop monthly, quarterly, annual, and ad hoc reports for federal stakeholders and project leadership. Translate complex data into actionable insights and recommendations for leadership and operational teams. Lead Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) activities, including quality reviews, monitoring activities, corrective action plans, and performance improvement initiatives. Support federal performance reviews, audits, monitoring visits, quality assessments, and contract compliance efforts. Collaborate with IT teams to support data integrations, API connections, workflow automation, data security, and reporting enhancements. Coordinate with legal, operations, intake, psychosocial, language services, and pro bono teams to ensure complete, accurate, and timely reporting across program functions. Supervise and mentor Data Reporting Lead and Quality Management Lead, Data Analysts, Reporting Specialists, and Quality Specialists. Provide leadership and guidance to staff responsible for data reporting, performance monitoring, and quality management activities. Experience working in Agile delivery environments, including backlog refinement, sprint planning, sprint reviews, demos, retrospectives, release readiness, or SAFe ceremonies. Strong technical writing skills, including the ability to document testing outcomes, data validation results, user feedback, risks, issues, and recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences. ICF’s Technology and Products team is seeking a On-call S oftware Engineer, Cloud Data Platform to help build, enhance, and support a cloud-hosted relational database platform for acoustic-telemetry fish-tracking research in California’s Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta. This role will focus on the core engineering work needed to turn post-processed fish detection data into reliable, usable data products, including ingestion pipelines, relational data models, validation logic, reporting views, exports, APIs, and production support. You will work alongside fish biologists, data scientists, senior engineers, and a state agency client to move the platform from design through go-live and into production support. This is a hands-on engineering role where you will contribute to platform design, implementation, and operations with guidance from senior technical leads. This is a remote, on-call role that provides flexibility to work from 0 to 40 hours per week. About On-Call Employment with ICF Given the seasonal and project-specific nature of this work, ICF often hires professionals as “On-Call” employees. On-Call employees are scheduled for work hours as they become available. ICF usually schedules work hours a few weeks ahead of time, and each on-call employee is free to accept or refuse the hours assigned to them in a given week. On-Call employees may work concurrent projects outside their ICF assignment as long as the outside work does not create a conflict of interest. Key Responsibilities Platform, data, and operations Translate scientific, regulatory, and analytical needs into clear technical requirements in partnership with biologists, data scientists, agency staff, client stakeholders, and senior technical team members. Contribute to the design, build, and support of a cloud-hosted relational database platform for acoustic-telemetry fish-tracking data. Build and maintain relational data models, ingestion workflows, ETL/ELT pipelines, validation logic, and data quality controls for high-volume telemetry detection data. Develop reporting views, aggregations, exports, APIs, and structured access patterns that support downstream modeling, analysis, and non-SQL users. Support platform performance, security, access controls, monitoring, backups, retention, documentation, and production operations during go-live and ongoing hosting. Help support a natural-language query interface by contributing to schema grounding, result validation, access safeguards, and accuracy guardrails. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field is required. 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including hands-on experience with relational database systems such as PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Azure SQL, or similar platforms. Hands-on experience supporting or contributing to cloud-hosted data platforms on AWS, Azure, or GCP. Strong SQL skills and experience with relational data modeling, data ingestion pipelines, ETL/ELT, and data quality validation. Proficiency in at least one modern backend language such as Python, TypeScript/Node, C#, or Java. Experience building or maintaining APIs, export capabilities, or reporting views that make structured data available to technical and non-technical users. Ability to work independently with guidance, collaborate on a remote team, and communicate clearly with non-engineering collaborators, including scientists, analysts, and client stakeholders. Preferred Skills / Experience Experience working with environmental, scientific, telemetry, sensor, time-series, or geospatial datasets; familiarity with acoustic telemetry or fisheries data is a plus. Exposure to large language models, natural-language interfaces, or tools that make structured data easier for non-technical users to access. Familiarity with public-sector clients or working under state or federal contracts. Experience with infrastructure as code, CI/CD, observability, monitoring, or operational support tooling. Experience supporting multidisciplinary teams that include biologists, researchers, quantitative modelers, analysts, data scientists, or subject matter experts. The Software Asset Management Product Owner - Enterprise SaaS functions as the product owner for a defined portfolio of enterprise SaaS applications (e.g., collaboration platforms, productivity tools, or designated enterprise SaaS systems). This role blends IT Asset Management (ITAM) disciplines—licensing, renewals, cost optimization, and compliance—with hands‑on application administration and engineering to ensure SaaS applications are secure, well‑integrated, and efficiently operated. As the technical steward for sanctioned SaaS tools, this role partners with Security, Identity, Procurement, Finance, and Enterprise Architects to ensure applications are securely onboarded, access is governed and auditable, and manual work is automated wherever possible, supporting modernization, security, and operational efficiency of the SaaS portfolio. Key Responsibilities 1. Product Ownership & Value Delivery ( ~ 35%) Own roadmap and backlog for assigned SaaS applications or ITAM tooling. Drive operational improvements through automation, standardized practices, and governance oversight. Balance compliance requirements with business productivity needs. Act as primary interface between business stakeholders and engineering/support teams. Define success metrics (adoption, cost efficiency, risk posture). Evaluate and vet new SaaS tools for technical compatibility, security posture, integration requirements, and administrative overhead prior to adoption. 2. Application Administration & Security Engineering (~35%) Serve as the technical application administrator for approved SaaS platforms, ensuring secure, scalable, and efficient day-to-day operations. Partner with Identity, Security, and other teams to configure and maintain: SSO and conditional access integrations MFA enforcement, admin role assignments, and security settings Automation workflows for SaaS administration, including license provisioning/deprovisioning, role assignments, and access reviews Implement and support least-privilege access models, including management of service accounts, service principals, secrets, and API permissions. Oversee and automate user lifecycle processes (joiner, mover, leaver), ensuring access provisioning aligns with role, policy, and audit requirements. Leverage AI, APIs, scripting, and low-code platforms to reduce manual administrative effort and improve operational consistency. Establish and document application administration standards, including admin ownership models, access review cadences, and secure configuration baselines. Act as an escalation point for complex application and access-related issues beyond Tier 1/2 support. 3. SaaS Financial & Lifecycle Management (~30%) Own the software lifecycle for defined portfolio of enterprise SaaS applications, from onboarding through renewal and retirement. Monitor application usage, license consumption, and spending to: Identify under‑utilization and seat reclamation opportunities Recommend license model changes and contract right‑sizing Lead renewal readiness by partnering with Finance and Procurement using historical usage and forward‑looking demand. Maintain a clean, authoritative SaaS inventory, including license entitlements, assigned users, admins, and integrations. Drive visibility and optimization of SaaS spend, utilization, and risk posture across the assigned portfolio. Support internal and external audits by performing periodic user access reviews and license compliance validations. Execute governance processes in alignment with ITAM program standards. Required Skills: 3+ years of experience in SaaS application administration, or IT Asset Management, with demonstrated hands-on technical depth. 3+ years of demonstrated experience configuring, securing, and integrating SaaS applications in an enterprise environment, including SSO, API connections, and admin console management. Strong understanding of software licensing models (named, concurrent, consumption, enterprise agreements). Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to connect usage, entitlement, and spend data into actionable insights and recommendations. Ability to maintain accurate configuration and inventory data across multiple platforms, and to identify discrepancies through data analysis and system queries. Demonstrated initiative in adopting and applying emerging technologies, including AI and automation tooling, to streamline operations and improve decision-making. Desired Skills & Experience Working knowledge of: ITAM or SAM tooling CMDB or application inventory platforms Experience with: SSO technologies (SAML, OAuth, OpenID Connect) Identity platforms (e.g., Entra ID / Azure AD) Familiarity with: Service principals, API permissions, Graph‑style access models SaaS security configurations and vendor admin consoles Experience automating workflows using scripting, APIs, Power Platform, or similar tools. Bachelor’s degree Experience building dashboards and reports (Excel and/or BI tools) and communicating results to non-technical stakeholders. Comfortable operating at the intersection of governance, engineering, and cost optimization. Hands on experience supporting SOX, ITGC, or access review processes. ICF is seeking a Digital and Social Media Specialist to support a marketing and communications campaign through the development, execution, management, and evaluation of digital and social media strategies. The successful candidate will help advance campaign goals by creating compelling digital content, implementing social media marketing tactics, increasing audience engagement, driving website traffic, and supporting outreach to target populations. This role requires a communications professional with strong writing, editing, digital content development, social media listening, engagement tool, and social media management experience. The Digital and Social Media Specialist will support campaign strategy, messaging, content planning, audience engagement, digital outreach, performance tracking, and reporting. The ideal candidate understands platform-specific best practices, content formats, social media algorithms, audience behavior, social media listening and engagement tools, and how to use data to improve campaign effectiveness. Develop, manage, and optimize high-profile social media content aligned with campaign goals, messaging, audiences, and brand requirements. Prepare campaign performance summaries, metrics updates, insights, and recommendations in collaboration with communications, creative, technical, analytics, and client-facing teams. Familiarity with paid, organic, and integrated digital media strategies. Experience applying accessibility, plain language, and inclusive communications best practices. We are seeking a Lead Energy Engineer to support multiple energy efficiency programs in Texas. The Lead Energy Engineer will lead technical development and oversee execution of complex energy efficiency and decarbonization projects for utility programs that encourage energy efficiency in commercial, schools, data centers, government buildings and industrial facilities. This individual will be a critical member of the team and will utilize a unique combination of interpersonal and analytical skills to be successful and ensure client satisfaction. Provide guidance to engineering staff on best practices, baseline selection for existing buildings and new construction and preparing M&V plans for energy savings verification. Assess feasibility for new energy efficiency measures or disruptive technologies, act as a liaison to clients to develop pilot studies and potential deemed savings methodologies. Develop and/or review spreadsheet and/or regression models for new and existing technologies. Conduct on-site energy assessments and analyze the energy performance of commercial buildings to determine cost-effective energy efficiency upgrades. You will be responsible for helping government clients plan, manage, and execute complex digital transformation and platform modernization initiatives using ServiceNow ITSM and ITOM capabilities. As a motivated ServiceNow Business Analyst, you play a pivotal role in successfully supporting ServiceNow delivery by gathering requirements, analyzing business processes, documenting user stories and acceptance criteria, and helping teams translate mission and operational needs into scalable ServiceNow solutions. Your facilitation, documentation, stakeholder engagement, and analytical skills will contribute significantly to the success of our projects and the satisfaction of our clients. You will be part of an established team supporting federal client delivery within the United States. The Team: ICF teams support federal clients seeking to leverage the ServiceNow platform to achieve greater operational efficiencies through automation, real-time reporting and analytics, improved staff productivity, and enhanced end-user experiences. The goal is to help clients use ServiceNow to improve service management processes, better understand operational data, modernize workflows, and support more effective business operations. The Work The qualified candidate will support ServiceNow ITSM and ITOM requirements analysis, process improvement, Agile delivery, backlog readiness, user acceptance testing, and stakeholder coordination. Position Responsibilities: Requirements Elicitation: Work closely with government stakeholders, product owners, Project Managers, ServiceNow architects, developers, testers, and administrators to gather, analyze, document, and validate business and functional requirements. Business Process Analysis: Analyze current-state and future-state service management processes and identify opportunities for automation, workflow improvement, reporting enhancements, and better user experience. User Stories and Acceptance Criteria: Translate business needs into user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, functional specifications, mockups, and supporting documentation. ITSM Support: Support requirements for ITSM applications such as Incident, Problem, Change, Request, Knowledge, Service Catalog, service-level management, and operational reporting. ITOM Support: Support requirements related to CMDB, Discovery, Service Mapping, Event Management, operational data quality, and service visibility. Agile Delivery Support: Participate in Agile ceremonies, backlog grooming, sprint planning, demos, retrospectives, and requirements readiness activities. Stakeholder Collaboration: Facilitate workshops, working sessions, JAD sessions, demos, and requirements review meetings with business and technical stakeholders. Documentation: Create and maintain BRDs, user stories, acceptance criteria, process maps, SOPs, decision logs, meeting notes, training materials, and release support documentation. Testing and Quality Assurance Support: Support test case development, UAT planning, defect review, requirements traceability, validation activities, and release readiness. Change Management and Training Support: Assist with user communications, training materials, stakeholder demos, and transition activities to support adoption of ServiceNow capabilities. Risk and Dependency Management: Identify requirements gaps, dependencies, assumptions, risks, and open decisions. Escalate issues appropriately and help facilitate timely resolution. Collaboration and Communication: Communicate effectively with technical and non-technical audiences and ensure requirements remain aligned to business outcomes, scope, and platform constraints. Required Skills: 3+ years of experience as a Business Analyst supporting software delivery, workflow modernization, enterprise platforms, or IT service management initiatives. 3+ years of experience eliciting, analyzing, documenting, and refining requirements in Agile/Scrum or Kanban delivery environments. 3+ years of experience facilitating stakeholder interviews, requirements sessions, design workshops, JAD sessions, demos, or comparable collaborative discovery activities. Experience supporting ServiceNow projects or comparable enterprise workflow platform initiatives. Experience with ServiceNow ITSM workflows, terminology, and service management processes. Experience with ServiceNow ITOM concepts such as CMDB, Discovery, Service Mapping, Event Management, operational data, or service dependency mapping. Experience creating user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, workflow diagrams, requirements traceability, and functional documentation. Experience using Agile collaboration tools such as ServiceNow Agile Development, Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or similar tools. Strong analytical, facilitation, problem-solving, documentation, and stakeholder management skills. Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. MUST RESIDE IN THE United States (U.S.) and the work MUST BE PERFORMED in the United States (U.S.), as this work is for a federal contract and laws do apply. Knowledge of ITSM, ITOM, CMDB, Service Portal, ITIL-aligned processes, and platform-based modernization. Knowledge of ServiceNow’s Generative AI capabilities like Now Assist. Experience supporting UAT, release planning, training, change management, or production support transition activities. The Federal Budget Coordinator / Cost Analyst is responsible for overseeing planning, execution, monitoring, and reporting of budgets and costs for federally funded programs and contracts. This role ensures financial integrity, regulatory compliance, and accurate cost accounting in accordance with federal regulations, contract requirements, and generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). The position serves as a key liaison between USPS leadership, finance, and external stakeholders to support sound fiscal management and audit readiness. Key Responsibilities Federal Budget Coordination Develop, manage, and monitor program and contract budgets across multiple funding sources and fiscal years. Track obligations, expenditures, burn rates, and forecasts to ensure alignment with approved funding levels and contract terms. Prepare budget justifications, estimates at completion (EACs), and variance analyses; identify risks and recommend corrective actions. Support budget modifications, re-baseline efforts, and funding realignments in coordination with program and contracting staff. Cost Accounting & Financial Controls Apply cost accounting principles to ensure accurate allocation, allowability, and documentation of direct and indirect costs. Review and reconcile labor, subcontractor, vendor, and other direct charges against approved budgets and cost structures. Maintain audit-ready financial records, including supporting documentation for invoices, accruals, and cost transfers. Support monthly close activities, reconciliations, and financial reporting in coordination with corporate finance teams. Assist with internal and external audits, monitoring reviews, and responses to findings or data requests. Reporting & Stakeholder Support Prepare and deliver routine and ad hoc financial reports for program leadership, corporate finance, and government clients. Serve as a financial advisor to project managers, providing guidance on budgeting, cost controls, and financial decision-making. Contribute to the development and improvement of financial policies, procedures, templates, and tracking tools. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree Minimum of 3 years of experience with financial analysis related to IT programs US Citizenship required by federal contract Additional Qualifications Demonstrated experience supporting budgets and cost accounting for federal contracts or federally funded programs. Working knowledge of GAAP and federal financial compliance requirements. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial data and communicate results clearly. Preferred Qualifications Experience with government contracting or grant environments (e.g., cost-reimbursable, T&M, FFP). Familiarity with USPS financial systems, project accounting tools, and advanced Excel or reporting platforms. CPA, CMA, or similar professional certification (or progress toward certification). The Technical Writer is responsible for research, technical writing, comprehensive editorial refinement, and project management of a wide range of materials, including feature articles, technical reports, white papers, and related communications products. This role translates technical jargon, data, and complex research into clear, authoritative, and accessible content for diverse audiences. The writer manages the full document lifecycle, from initial research and subject matter expert interviews through final production, ensuring technical accuracy, editorial quality, and compliance with Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) requirements. Job Description Content Development & Technical Writing: Research and write original content for feature articles, technical reports, white papers, newsletters, and other technical communications. Collaborate closely with engineers, researchers, developers, and other technical staff to translate complex concepts into clear, concise content. Substantive Editing & Quality Assurance: Provide comprehensive editorial support across all stages of production for print and electronic materials. Edit, rephrase, and rewrite content as needed to improve logical flow, coherence, organization, grammar, spelling, and formatting. Technical Accuracy & Fact-Checking: Verify technical accuracy using existing materials, subject matter expert interviews, research, and other appropriate sources. Perform fact-checking, reference checking, and data verification and ensure tables, schematics, and other supporting information are accurately integrated with the text. Compliance & Style Management: Ensure content complies with applicable FHWA and federal requirements, including the GPO Style Manual, the Chicago Manual of Style, and Section 508 accessibility requirements. Manage copyright and permission clearances as needed. Document Lifecycle Management: Work independently to manage documents and articles from initial development through final publication. Maintain quality assurance and version control and navigate multiple review and revision cycles with technical experts and other stakeholders. Location: Remote within the United States. Conducting subject matter research, interviewing technical experts, verifying facts and references, and ensuring technical accuracy. 5-10 years’ experience in applying major style guides and editorial standards, including Section 508 compliance. This role is contingent upon a contract award. ICF is seeking an IAM Lead to architect, implement, and operate the identity and access management platform for a federal technology program. Reporting to engineering leadership, this role is the subject matter authority on how users, devices, and applications authenticate and are authorized across a cloud-first, Zero Trust environment. The IAM Lead owns the full identity lifecycle, from onboarding automation to privileged access controls to external identity federation. The ideal candidate is a senior identity engineer who has built and operated IAM programs in federal cloud environments. This is a deeply technical role. The right candidate understands not just the tooling but the underlying standards, can implement NIST identity assurance requirements, and can hold their own with cybersecurity and enterprise architecture teams on access policy design. Job Location: This is a remote-friendly position with occasional onsite requirements in the Washington, DC Metro area. This position requires that the job be performed in the United States. If you accept this position, you should note that ICF does monitor employee work locations and blocks access from foreign locations/foreign IP addresses and also prohibits personal VPN connections. What You'll Be Doing Architect, configure, and maintain identity platforms including Entra ID, Entra External ID, and Okta, covering authentication, authorization, provisioning, and lifecycle management across all users, applications, and devices. Configure and enforce phishing-resistant authentication for all users, including passkeys, FIDO2 security keys, WebAuthn , and biometrics. Drive the transition away from legacy authentication methods toward a fully passwordless posture. Define and implement Zero Trust access rules based on user risk, device health, location, and behavior using risk-based and conditional access policies. Design, configure, and operate authorization models including RBAC, PBAC, and ABAC, with fine-grained permissions and attribute-based access rules aligned to job function and least-privilege principles. Manage privileged accounts and administrative roles using privileged access management (PAM) and just-in-time elevation, ensuring that standing admin access is minimized and all elevated access is logged and time-bound. Build and maintain HR-driven joiner, mover, and leaver automation, including automated provisioning, license assignment, role changes, access revocation, and data archival triggered by HR system events. Federate external identities including partners, contractors, and external collaborators using Entra External ID or equivalent, including self-service registration, verification workflows, and consent management. Configure identity proofing and verification to NIST IAL and AAL levels where required , coordinating with cybersecurity and compliance teams on assurance requirements. Integrate applications and APIs with identity platforms using OIDC, OAuth2, SAML, and SCIM for single sign-on and automated provisioning. Monitor sign-in activity, risk signals, and anomalies. Respond to identity-related incidents including account takeover, phishing, access abuse, and fraud in coordination with the cybersecurity team. Maintain identity data quality and consistency across directories, HR systems, and applications, including synchronization, schema management, and attribute mapping. Support compliance and audit activities by producing access reports, certifications, attestations, and evidence of controls. Document identity architectures, configurations, standards, and runbooks. Provide guidance to application teams on how to onboard to central identity platforms and implement authentication best practices. Minimum Requirements Bachelor's degree or equivalent 7+ years of experience in identity and access management engineering or a related discipline 3+ years of hands-on experience designing and operating Entra ID or Okta in production environments, including conditional access, lifecycle management, and federation 2+ years implementing PAM solutions and just-in-time elevation controls for privileged accounts 2+ years configuring authorization models including RBAC, PBAC, or ABAC in enterprise environments 2+ years supporting federal IT programs in HHS, NIH, FDA, or other health-focused agencies U .S . Working at ICF means applying a passion for meaningful work with intellectual rigor to help solve the leading issues of our day. As a Technical Editor, you will lead and oversee the editorial process for high-stakes technical documentation and publications. You will collaborate with program managers, subject matter experts, technical staff, and leadership to transform complex technical information, raw data, and engineering terminology into clear, accurate, authoritative, and accessible products for transportation practitioners, agency stakeholders, and the traveling public. The Technical Editor will provide substantive and technical editing, ensure consistency and quality across large-scale programs, and manage documents throughout the full editorial lifecycle-from initial outline and development through final publication, including online and web publishing. The position will also provide editorial leadership and guidance to junior staff and other members of the project team. This role will be supported remotely and may require infrequent in-person meetings at the client site in McLean, VA. What You’ll Be Doing: Lead the editorial process for complex, high-visibility technical documents, reports, manuals, publications, and web-based products. Perform substantive and technical editing to improve organization, clarity, readability, accuracy, consistency, and usability. Transform raw data, engineering terminology, and highly technical subject matter into clear, authoritative content appropriate for intended audiences. Work closely with subject matter experts to verify technical accuracy while preserving the integrity and meaning of technical information. Translate complex technical concepts and terminology into plain language when appropriate. Ensure documents comply with agency and department style guides, publication standards, branding requirements, and established editorial practices. Apply expert knowledge of the U.S. Government Publishing Office (GPO) Style Manual to federal publications and other client deliverables. Conduct reference checking, fact checking, and editorial quality assurance and quality control. Review content for copyright compliance and appropriate attribution and use of source materials. Research, outline, edit, and support the development of reports and other products addressing complex technical concepts. Manage the full lifecycle of documents from outline and initial drafts through reviews, revisions, final production, and publication. Coordinate multiple authors, reviewers, subject matter experts, and stakeholders to maintain editorial consistency across large-scale programs. Establish and maintain consistent terminology, editorial conventions, and style across related products and publications. Perform copy editing, proofreading, document formatting, and final publication reviews. Support Section 508 accessibility and quality-control activities and ensure products comply with applicable agency accessibility guidance. Work with Microsoft Office applications and PDF/document-production tools to review, edit, format, and finalize publications. Provide editorial direction, mentoring, and quality oversight to junior editors and other project staff. Manage multiple assignments and deadlines independently while maintaining consistently high editorial standards. Basic Qualifications: Master's degree in English, Journalism, or a technical field. 10+ years of experience editing and reviewing technical documents, managing projects, and supervising staff. 10+ years of experience with GPO Style Manual and government publishing standards, document quality control, and Microsoft Word and PowerPoint. Have the ability to obtain a government clearance if required. Preferred Qualifications: Experience supporting federal government agencies and federal publications. Transportation industry experience, particularly in highway and surface transportation. Experience editing engineering, research, scientific, policy, or other highly technical documentation. Experience with Adobe Acrobat Pro, CommonLook, and Section 508 accessibility requirements. Familiarity with online and web publishing. Familiarity with collaboration and project-management tools such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Smartsheet, Basecamp, and Trello. Professional Skills: Exceptional command of grammar, syntax, usage, punctuation, style, and editorial conventions. Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate, consistent, high-quality publications. Strong editorial judgment and the ability to identify and resolve substantive issues in complex technical content. Ability to understand technical concepts quickly and communicate them clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and organizational communication skills. Strong leadership and mentoring skills, with the ability to provide clear and constructive editorial guidance. Self-directed, resourceful problem solver with the ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment. Proven ability to manage competing priorities, perspectives, deadlines, and stakeholder needs. Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams. Ability to diplomatically reconcile conflicting reviewer comments and editorial perspectives while maintaining document quality and technical integrity. Flexibility and willingness to adapt to changing priorities and project requirements. The Work: ICF is seeking an experienced Systems Engineer to support the design, implementation, operation, and maintenance of enterprise network infrastructure supporting critical federal programs. This role requires strong technical expertise in network engineering, systems administration, troubleshooting, and infrastructure modernization within complex enterprise environments. Job Location: This position is remote and requires that the job be performed in the United States. If you accept this position, you should note that ICF monitors employee work locations and blocks access from foreign locations/foreign IP addresses and prohibits personal VPN connections. Our core work hours are 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM Eastern Time, with flexibility to start earlier or work later depending on your time zone. Please note that project meetings may occasionally begin before 10:00 AM Eastern to accommodate client requirements. Limited travel may be required for customer meetings, infrastructure deployments, or team collaboration. What You Will Do: The selected candidate will support the administration, maintenance, and enhancement of enterprise network infrastructure while ensuring high availability and operational performance. The Systems Engineer will perform systems engineering activities across network hardware, operating systems, and communication technologies while providing technical support, troubleshooting complex issues, and assisting with infrastructure modernization initiatives. This individual will work closely with network engineers, system administrators, cybersecurity personnel, and project leadership to maintain secure and reliable IT operations. Investigate, analyze, recommend, configure, install, and test new network hardware, software, and infrastructure components. Provide day-to-day operational support for enterprise network infrastructure and operating systems. Monitor system utilization, network performance, and response times to ensure optimal system availability. Diagnose and resolve complex network, communications, and infrastructure issues. Troubleshoot network connectivity at both the physical and logical layers using network measurement tools and diagnostic software. Perform hardware testing, configuration validation, and communication protocol analysis. Participate in the planning, design, technical review, implementation, and deployment of new network infrastructure and operating systems. Support voice and data communication networks, ensuring reliable and secure network services. Maintain network infrastructure standards, configurations, and documentation. Configure, monitor, and support TCP/IP networking and other enterprise communication protocols. Collaborate with cybersecurity, systems administration, and engineering teams to ensure secure network operations. Develop and maintain technical documentation, network diagrams, standard operating procedures, and system configurations. Support infrastructure modernization, performance optimization, and continuous improvement initiatives. ICF is seeking a senior aviation technical adviser to strengthen our aircraft leasing and technical advisory capability. The role is suited to an experienced aviation professional with deep knowledge of aircraft assets, lease structures, maintenance obligations, technical records and aircraft lifecycle considerations. The successful candidate will have the judgement to challenge assumptions, resolve complex technical questions, translate detailed analysis into commercially relevant advice, direct analytical and delivery teams, and take accountability for the technical quality of client work. In this role, you will lead fast-paced, complex and recurring engagements across the aircraft lifecycle, spanning leasing, maintenance, appraisals, asset management, technical due diligence and selected expert-witness assignments. You will have the opportunity to shape ICF’s aircraft technical capability, lead an international delivery team and work across leasing, maintenance, valuation, asset management and transaction assignments. What you will do Lead technical delivery on aviation finance, aircraft leasing, maintenance, valuation support, appraisal and technical due diligence engagements. Set the technical and analytical approach on key projects, challenge assumptions and take accountability for accurate, commercially robust and client-ready outputs. Lead or directly undertake the most complex elements of assignments where senior technical judgement is required. Direct and quality-assure work across lease reviews, maintenance cash-flow analysis, aircraft, engine and inventory valuations, fleet analysis, technical records, lease returns and transaction support. Provide end-to-end oversight of key assignments, ensuring clear scope and ownership, appropriate project set-up, disciplined work planning, visible client communications, timely technical review, accurate project documentation and effective management of budget and delivery risk. Guide analysts and multi-location delivery teams, resolving technical questions, providing constructive review and strengthening team capability. Advise clients on aircraft leasing, maintenance reserves, return conditions, MRO, asset management and aircraft lifecycle matters, resolving or escalating technical and delivery issues promptly. Develop, embed and maintain the methodologies, tools, templates and quality standards used across aircraft finance and technical advisory assignments. Develop team capability through structured coaching, technical review, practical training and progressive delegation of responsibility. Contribute technical expertise to proposals, client development and industry activity. What we are looking for Significant experience in aircraft leasing, lease management, aviation finance, aviation technical advisory, MRO, maintenance planning, asset management, appraisal support or a related aviation field. Deep understanding of aircraft leases, maintenance reserves, return conditions, technical records, fleet maintenance obligations and aircraft lifecycle considerations. Demonstrated experience leading and quality-assuring complex analysis involving aircraft and engine assets, leases, maintenance cash flows, valuations or technical due diligence. Ability to supervise junior team members and multi-location delivery teams, providing clear technical direction and constructive feedback. Credibility and confidence to advise senior clients on complex technical and commercial aviation matters. Understanding of the requirements of lessors, airlines, lenders, investors and MRO providers in relation to aircraft assets. Excellent judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to identify technical risks, analytical inconsistencies and commercial implications. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex analysis into clear client advice. Ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines, locations and cultures. Willingness to travel for client meetings, inspections and project work as required. Preferred experience Typically 12+ years of relevant experience in aircraft leasing, aircraft appraisal, asset management, technical advisory, or airline fleet and lease management. Experience working with aircraft lessors, lenders, investors, airlines, MROs, OEMs or technical service providers. Experience with aircraft appraisals, portfolio valuations, maintenance cash-flow forecasting, lease return and redelivery analysis, technical due diligence, asset-backed financing or aircraft transaction support. Experience reviewing lease documents, technical records, maintenance status reports, inspection outputs or maintenance-related assumptions used in valuation or transaction work. ISTAT Appraiser or ISTAT Candidate status would be advantageous. Professional experience in aircraft engineering, CAMO, maintenance planning, technical records or aircraft asset management would also be valuable. Experience developing technical methodologies, training materials, quality-control processes or analytical tools. Established network and credibility within the aviation leasing, maintenance, aircraft finance or technical advisory community. About ICF Aviation: ICF’s aviation practice is one of the world's largest specialist aviation consulting teams. We advise airlines, airports, investors, lessors, lenders, governments, manufacturers and service providers on strategic, financial, operational and technical challenges across the global aviation market. Our aircraft finance work includes support for cash-flow forecasts underpinning asset-backed securitisations, tangible and intangible aviation asset valuations, on-site audits, restructurings, due diligence, lease restructuring and renegotiations, and emerging themes such as sustainable finance and new aircraft technologies. From our offices in the US, UK, India and Spain, we work together as a single global team to deliver practical, technically grounded advice to aviation clients. This role is contingent upon a contract award. ICF is seeking a Cloud Platform Engineer to deploy, configure, and maintain cloud infrastructure for a federal technology program. Reporting to the Cloud / Enterprise Architecture Lead, this role is responsible for building and operating the multi-cloud landing zone environment using infrastructure-as-code and DevSecOps practices. Where the EA Lead sets architecture standards and policy, this role executes and maintains them in production. The ideal candidate is a hands-on cloud infrastructure engineer who writes automation before clicking buttons and treats configuration as code. The right candidate has deployed and operated cloud landing zones in federal environments and is comfortable working across Azure, AWS, and GCP with consistent tooling and governance discipline. Job Location: This is a remote-friendly position with occasional onsite requirements in the Washington, DC Metro area. This position requires that the job be performed in the United States. If you accept this position, you should note that ICF does monitor employee work locations and blocks access from foreign locations/foreign IP addresses and also prohibits personal VPN connections. What You'll Be Doing Deploy and manage cloud landing zone architectures across Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud Platform using repeatable, automated provisioning with identity-first controls, guardrails, network security, and policy enforcement. Implement infrastructure and policy as code using IaC templates, GitHub Actions, and CI/CD pipelines so environments can be created, updated, and audited consistently and without manual intervention. Build and maintain system integrations using APIs, SDKs, webhooks, and event streams, with proper secrets management, least-privilege scoping, error handling, and logging. Deploy and manage Azure Virtual Desktop for remote access scenarios and specific user personas. Manage DNS-as-code for all agency platforms and services, including certificates and related configurations. Integrate platform logs, alerts, and risk signals into central monitoring tools, and use automation to flag misconfigurations, risky behavior, and suspicious activity. Perform quarterly reviews of cloud environment configurations against security baselines and compliance requirements, using compliance-as-code tooling where available. Coordinate with identity, device, and cybersecurity teams to ensure cloud access policies, device compliance rules, and conditional access work together as part of a consistent Zero Trust model. Maintain documentation of cloud architectures, configuration baselines, runbooks, and operational procedures so others can safely operate and extend the environment. Resolve complex cloud platform issues escalated from operations and service desk teams. Direct cloud governance (AWS Orgs/SCPs; Azure Mgmt Groups/Policy; tagging & cost allocation) and audit adherence. Define the strategy for AI‑driven automation and observability (e.g., Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry) and sequence use‑cases that deliver measurable impact. Be accountable for day‑to‑day operations outcomes (patching, backups/restore, capacity, performance, monitoring/alerting) delivered by teams and vendors, with clear KPIs and review cadences. Govern ITIL 4 processes (incident, change/CAB, problem, request) with targets for MTTR, change success rate, and RCA quality. Ensure a 24/7 support model (runbooks/playbooks, on‑call rotations) is funded, staffed, tested, and reviewed via post‑incident governance; mandate chaos engineering and DR test schedules with executive readouts. Champion integration of AI agents into operations; approve guardrails for automated remediation and anomaly detection. Security & Compliance Ensure defensible controls aligned to NIST 800‑53, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and (where applicable) FedRAMP, with continuous control monitoring and evidence management. Direct continuous compliance via AWS Config, Azure Policy, CIS Benchmarks, Well‑Architected/CAF; review exceptions and drive closure. Partner with Security/Compliance leadership on audits, findings, and corrective action plans. Govern secure AI workload deployment and ensure adherence to emerging AI governance frameworks with NIST/ISO/FedRAMP alignment. POSITION SUMMARY: Under the general direction of the Manager of Revenue Integrity, the Senior Coding and Revenue Integrity Analyst exists to ensure compliant charge capture and revenue tracking for both Boston Medical Center (BMC) and the professional Boston University Medical Group (BUMG) revenue. Operating under limited supervision and working independently, this role monitors regulatory changes, payer requirements, and revenue integrity policies to support compliant coding and billing practices across the enterprise. The position functions as a critical analytical liaison across both hospital and professional billing environments, performing comprehensive reimbursement analysis and developing detailed resolution plans to mitigate institutional revenue leakage. This role drives cross-functional collaboration and fosters constructive relationships between clinical revenue-producing departments and core revenue cycle teams to proactively resolve workflow deficiencies. Position : Senior Coding / Revenue Integrity Analyst Department : Revenue Integrity Schedule : Full Time Location: Remote with the occasional need to visit onsite ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES / DUTIES: Revenue Cycle Initiative Leadership: Leads complex revenue cycle initiatives and large-scale optimization projects across high-revenue-generating or at-risk clinical departments to improve overall revenue integrity, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance. Project Work Plan Management: Develops and executes detailed project work plans, timelines, and resolution frameworks for complex, multi-departmental revenue initiatives with limited managerial oversight to ensure timely delivery of operational goals. Epic System Workflow Validation: Monitors, audits, and validates active charging workflows within Epic and intersecting third-party charging interfaces to ensure technical baseline accuracy and appropriate system build configuration. Root Cause Data Analysis: Analyzes Epic work queue data and revenue performance metrics to execute structural root cause analysis, identify localized workflow deficiencies, and present formalized interpretations and actionable findings to leadership. Departmental Sourcing Support: Manages charging, coding, and billing processes within clinical departments by auditing revenue-producing activities to verify compliance with evolving government regulations and third-party payer contract requirements. Cross-Functional Stakeholder Collaboration: Partners with departmental stakeholders, finance leaders, and revenue cycle teams to assess active clinical workflows, troubleshoot system issues, and deliver targeted training and analytical feedback. Subject Matter Expertise & Escalation Support: Serves as the primary functional subject matter expert and institutional liaison for charge capture, supporting complex escalation issues and guiding cross-functional revenue cycle partners. (The above statements in this job description are intended to depict the general nature and level of work assigned to the employee(s) in this job. The above is not intended to represent an exhaustive list of accountable duties and responsibilities required). JOB REQUIREMENTS REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Associate’s degree in Business, Healthcare, or a related field; and at least five (5) years of healthcare experience, including at least two years in an active role involving coding, auditing, finance, revenue cycle management, and/or physician billing (preferably within an Academic Medical Center setting); or equivalent combination of education and experience . PREFERRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: A Bachelor’s degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, or a closely related field, combined with five (5) or more years of progressive revenue integrity experience within a matrixed health system. CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS REQUIRED: Certified Professional Coder (CPC), Certified Coding Specialist – Physician-based (CCS-P), or Certified Professional Medical Auditor (CPMA). KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES (KSAs): Advanced Process and Root Cause Analysis: Advanced proficiency in process analysis, troubleshooting, and database investigation to structurally isolate billing deficiencies and engineer actionable solutions. Healthcare Revenue Cycle Principles: Strong working knowledge of materials management, purchasing, contracting, and vendor management structures as they intersect with hospital charging systems, Epic, and nThrive applications. Objective Data Synthesization: Advanced analytical skills to evaluate complex utilization datasets from multiple disparate sources, develop summary metrics, and translate findings into current, accurate procurement and billing recommendations. Strategic Communication and Presentation: Superior written and verbal communication skills, including the objective ability to present complex fiscal trends, regulatory interpretations, and systemic recommendations to senior administrative and physician leadership. Independent Project Management: Strong organizational and time management skills to manage deadlines, prioritize personal workloads, and autonomously drive multiple concurrent project plans. Stakeholder Influence and Interviewing: Strong active listening and interviewing skills to gather relevant workflow data from clinical personnel and establish collaborative working relationships across diverse medical and administrative teams. Office Application Competency: Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Forms, to execute automated operational reporting and project tracking. Compensation Range: $78,000.00- $113,000.00 This range offers an estimate based on the minimum job qualifications. However, our approach to determining base pay is comprehensive, and a broad range of factors is considered when making an offer. This includes education, experience, skills, and certifications/licensures as they directly relate to position requirements; as well as business/organizational needs, internal equity, and market-competitiveness. In addition, BMCHS offers generous total compensation that includes, but is not limited to, benefits (medical, dental, vision, pharmacy), discretionary annual bonuses and merit increases, Flexible Spending Accounts, 403(b) savings matches, paid time off, career advancement opportunities, and resources to support employee and family well-being. NOTE : This range is based on Boston-area data, and is subject to modification based on geographic location. Cyber Detection & Response Automation Engineer The Cyber Detection & Response Automation Engineer is responsible for building the automation, orchestration, and AI-driven capabilities that power the organization's detection and response function. This role treats the SIEM as one component in a broader automation ecosystem — the primary focus is designing workflows, integrations, and intelligent tooling that reduce manual analyst effort, accelerate response, and scale detection coverage. The ideal candidate is an automation/orchestration engineer with a security background: comfortable building integrations and pipelines across multiple tools, applying AI/ML or LLM-assisted techniques to triage and enrichment, and engineering detection logic. This person will also maintain a working level of SIEM platform administration — data onboarding, health, and configuration — to support the automation and detection layers built on top of it, and will partner closely with Security Operations and the Detection Engineering Lead. What you'll be doing: Design, build, and maintain orchestration workflows and SOAR playbooks that automate triage, enrichment, containment, and response actions across the security tool stack. Apply AI/ML and LLM-assisted techniques (e.g., automated alert summarization, natural-language investigation assistance, anomaly scoring) to reduce analyst workload and speed decision-making. Develop and maintain Python-based integrations and APIs connecting the SIEM, SOAR, EDR, ticketing, threat intel, and cloud platforms into unified automated workflows. Design, build, and tune SIEM correlation rules, alerts, and detection use cases mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, with an eye toward which detections can be paired with automated response. Own core SIEM administration tasks needed to support automation and detection: data source onboarding, index/data model health, log ingestion monitoring, and configuration management. Build and maintain custom field extractions, parsers, and content packs to ensure new data sources are automation- and detection-ready. Continuously tune detections and automation logic to improve signal-to-noise ratio, reduce false positives, and reduce mean-time-to-respond (MTTR). Create dashboards and reporting that measure automation coverage, orchestration reliability, AI-assisted triage accuracy, and detection effectiveness. Apply CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code practices to manage detection content, playbooks, and integrations as versioned, testable code. Evaluate and pilot new automation, orchestration, and AI tooling to expand the detection and response automation footprint. What we'll want you to have: 5+ years building automation, orchestration, or SOAR playbooks in a cyber security or SOC environment. 3+ years of SIEM engineering or administration experience - data onboarding, correlation rule development, platform configuration. Strong Python (or comparable scripting) skills; experience building APIs/integrations across security and IT tooling. Hands-on experience with AI/ML or LLM-based tooling applied to security use cases - triage, summarization, enrichment, and/or anomaly detection; experience building such capability strongly preferred. Working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK and experience mapping detections/automation to adversary tactics and techniques. Experience with a SOAR or security orchestration platform (e.g., NG-SIEM Fusion, Splunk SOAR, Palo Alto XSOAR, Tines, or similar). Cloud security experience (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including automation for ingesting and processing security data from cloud sources. Experience with CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, and version-controlling detection/automation content. Familiarity with containerized and serverless environments and their automation/logging considerations. SIEM, SOAR, or security automation platform certification preferred. Regulatory compliance experience a plus.
